newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven says Q1 revenue ahead of yr ago.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven says Q1 revenue ahead of yr ago.

text.p: Television operator Seven Network Ltd said on Thursday sales revenue for the first quarter of the current 1996/97 fiscal year was running ahead of the corresponding period a year ago, despite a tight advertising market.
"We are up on last year," Seven chairman Kerry Stokes told reporters after the company's annual general meeting.

He said later he was referring to revenues only and that market conditions were very tough and the outlook subdued, unless the Reserve Bank of Australia eased monetary policy and boosted business confidence.

"The first quarter has been up to budget but very tough," he said. "Advertising is very tight and we are pleased with the (market) share. The market out there generally, the economy, is slowing down. Everybody's feeling it...," Stokes said.
Stokes said that fully franked dividends were unlikely to be paid for another three years
"We don't pay tax at this stage. We don't wish to have a dividend policy which declines as we take tax into account," he told the annual meeting earlier.
Stokes said the company would be paying increased taxes over the next two or three years.
Seven paid an unfranked dividend of 17.5 cents per share in the year to June 30, 1996.
